record.what_it_does: Salesforce B2C Commerce Cloud: enterprise ecommerce platform with Shopper and Admin REST APIs (SCAPI).
record.auth_notes: Admin APIs: API clients are created in Account Manager. They use the client_credentials grant with client_secret_basic (the default), or private_key_jwt for certificate-based JWT Bearer authentication. The client also needs the 'Salesforce Commerce API' role with a tenant filter, plus sfcc.* scopes. Browser sign-in uses Authorization Code + PKCE, and the implicit flow is deprecated. Shopper APIs use SLAS (OAuth 2.1) tokens, either guest or registered, with PKCE for public clients or a secret for private clients. Each merchant tenant (short code, org/tenant ID) needs its own API client.
record.access_notes: You need a licensed B2C Commerce tenant (realm). Salesforce's Commerce pricing page lists B2C as 'Contact for pricing' and shows no free trial for B2C. The only no-cost offer is Commerce Foundations, which is CRM-embedded and needs Sales/Service Enterprise Edition. On-demand sandboxes are only available inside a licensed realm (or a partner realm through the Salesforce partner program). There is no self-serve developer tier.
record.api_breadth_notes: SCAPI has two parts. The Shopper APIs cover products, search, baskets, checkout, orders, customers, promotions and SLAS. The Admin APIs cover catalogs, products, inventory, pricing, promotions, orders, customers, CDN zones, SLAS admin and others. Legacy OCAPI is also available. The official B2C DX MCP docs say 'SCAPI code mode' exposes nearly 600 Commerce API operations.
record.mcp_notes: Official local server: npm package @salesforce/b2c-dx-mcp, run with npx -y @salesforce/b2c-dx-mcp@latest. Salesforce's PWA Kit docs title it 'B2C DX MCP Server (Developer Preview)'. It is developer-focused: docs search, cartridge/MRT deploy, debugging, WebDAV, CIP analytics, and SCAPI Admin and Shopper calls (~600 operations). Salesforce also offers a vendor-hosted B2C Commerce MCP Shopper Service (SSE, SLAS tokens) that is pilot-only, with access through your Salesforce account executive. Community servers exist (e.g. sfcc-dev-mcp, Cequence AI gateway).
record.blocker_notes: The API is public, well documented and has OpenAPI specs. However, you can only get a tenant or sandbox to build and test against through a Salesforce license (contact for pricing) or a partner realm. There is no free developer tier. Even with a tenant, each merchant has to provision its own Account Manager or SLAS client and share its tenant IDs, so there is no central OAuth app for multi-user connection. I could not confirm native outbound webhooks.
